title: Grateful Dead Live at Family Dog at the Great Highway on 1969-11-02
venue: Family Dog at the Great Highway
lineage: SBD > MR > C1 > DAT > Turtle Beach Fiji > SHN

ai_review.summary: Crystal‑clear Good Bear soundboard capture of a legendary 1969 Family Dog set – 30‑minute Dark Star with superb Eleven and Death Don't Have Mercy.
ai_review.review: The recording is praised as “the best sound quality” ever heard for this era, with crisp drums, clear bass and vivid Hammond tones. Musically the show shines around its marathon Dark Star (≈30 min), flowing into a stellar St. Stephen → The Eleven → Death Don't Have Mercy sequence, making it a must‑have despite being a partial set. Overall fans deem both the performance and the tape quality exceptional.

ai_rating.rationale: Over 30 reviews overwhelmingly rate the show 5 stars, highlighting iconic Dark Star and superb recording clarity; only a single low rating mentions it being a partial set, so combined show (70%) and recording (30%) scores yield a high overall rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Listeners repeatedly note crisp, crystal‑clear drums, superb bass definition and vivid Hammond organ; no significant drop‑outs or muffiness reported. The tape is a Good Bear sbd, regarded as one of the best‑sounding 1969 captures.

show_quality.setlist_flow: A powerful Dark Star opens the fragment, segues into St. Stephen → The Eleven → Death Don't, creating a high‑octane arc; the additional cuts (Cold Rain & Snow, Midnight Hour) round out the set with contrasting moods.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia’s guitar tone described as perfect and “deeply personal”; his vocal on Death Don't Have Mercy praised as soulful; melodic improvisation in Dark Star highlighted.
band_member_comments.Phil: Phil’s bass noted as ‘popping away’ with outstanding clarity, often called the best‑sound‑quality bass of the era.
band_member_comments.Keys: Tom (Hammond) singled out for his lush organ work; overall keyboard texture described as swirling and “crisp”.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill’s drumming, especially on The Eleven, praised as crystal clear and a highlight of the performance; percussion noted as remarkable.
